title: Golden session snapshots and multiplexed replay harness for multi-SDK contract tests
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Produce a reusable suite of 'golden session' snapshots and a multiplexed replay harness that lets Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs run deterministic contract checks against the Redwood API for streaming and non-streaming endpoints. The intent is to capture end-to-end binary and textual payloads (including interleaved control frames), preserve chunk boundaries, and provide time-offset variants so SDK retry and backpressure logic can be validated deterministically.

Motivation: Existing VCR-style fixtures in the repo are focused on HTTP request/response semantics and text-only streams. We need a more expressive canonical snapshot format for: large-token streaming, partial chunk flushes, websocket-like framed streams, and binary-encoded function-call payloads used by some SDK examples. This will reduce flakiness in SDK CI and catch multiplexing/regression bugs (racey retry logic, resumed KV cache misuse, token-count drift across languages).

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Snapshot format specification (human-readable JSON wrapper + base64 payload blobs) landed in docs/confluence and a machine-validate CLI.
- Harness that can replay a single snapshot concurrently to N SDK clients (simulating multiplexed sessions) and deterministically inject network events (latency spikes, partial frame drops).
- SDK contract tests for Python, TS, and Go that exercise: streaming generation with intermittent reconnects, function-calling with chunked JSON objects, and embedding/embedding-batch fallbacks.
- CI gates: contract tests run on PRs for each SDK; failures surface a deterministic replay artifact (S3 URL) and a short trace describing the mismatch.

Design notes:
- Snapshot file layout: top-level metadata (Redwood API version, model fingerprint, tokenizer hash, fixture timestamp), entries array where each entry is a single recorded frame with fields: direction, raw_base64_payload, mtimestamp_ns, connection_id. We explicitly record chunk boundaries and logical event ids so SDKs can assert on partial-delivery semantics.
- Replay server: lightweight Go binary that serves HTTP/WS endpoints; it can operate in three modes: record (live traffic capture), deterministic-replay (timing fidelity), fuzzed-replay (injects specified anomalies). Reuse the existing VCR adapter library where possible but extend it to preserve binary frames.
- Storage: canonical snapshots stored under s3://redwood-ci-fixtures/sdk-snapshots/{sha256}. Use signed expiring URLs for CI downloads.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Recording full binary payloads increases snapshot size; we will support both full and trimmed snapshots (trimmed removes non-essential payloads and keeps control frames).
- Time-deterministic replay requires freezing SDK timers in some languages; where SDKs cannot freeze, the harness will offer a shim and a best-effort mode.

Deliverables:
1) spec doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/Golden+Session+Snapshot+Spec
2) replay binary and test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-fixtures (PR #312)
3) three SDK contract test suites (python/ts/go) and CI matrix entries
4) migration guide for authors adding new snapshots
